name: Karplus-Strong pluck: noise-burst exciter into a key-tracked feedback delay with decay/damping and register compensation
goal: Build a playable Karplus-Strong plucked string in any modular/Web Audio environment: a short pink-noise burst (bandpass-filtered, velocity-scaled, optionally stereo) excites a delay line tuned to one period of the note (delay = 1/f, e.g. ~7.64 ms at C3; halve per octave up via 2^(−n/12) scaling), with feedback as decay and a low-pass in the loop as damping, both velocity-scalable and key-tracked to even out low-vs-high note ring time.

source.title: Karplus-Strong Synthesis in Bitwig Studio 3 - The Grid

prerequisites: Delay with feedback and an in-loop low-pass (or build one)
Noise source, bandpass/SVF filter, short envelope, velocity and key-pitch modulation, simple math (exp/invert)
constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.

Web Audio implementation note (not from transcript): DelayNode inside a cycle adds at least one 128-sample render quantum, which caps pitch (~345 Hz at 44.1 kHz) — use an AudioWorklet delay line for full range.
Keep exciter envelope shorter than the delay period for clean plucks; longer exciters become reverb-like swells.

steps.action: Build the exciter: pink noise (fuller than white) → bandpass SVF → a very short pluck envelope on level; add a velocity multiplier to scale excitation, and gain to keep long exciters in check.
steps.expect: Short noise click whose loudness follows velocity

steps.action: Feed the burst into a delay with built-in feedback and an in-loop low-pass. Set delay = one period of the target fundamental (7.64 ms ≈ C3) and feedback high so it keeps resonating.
steps.expect: Pitched pluck at C3 regardless of key

steps.action: Key-track the delay: delay time must scale by 2^(−n/12) (n = semitones from the reference). Going up an octave halves delay; down an octave doubles it. Convert the note-pitch value to that factor (exp base 2, invert, offset so the reference note = no change) before feeding the delay-time modulation.
steps.expect: Correct pitches up and down the keyboard (not barely changing)

steps.action: Exciter variations: use the envelope itself as the exciter (attack time changes tone like pluck position); widen the noise stereo for a lush tone; long exciter envelopes give a reverb-like bloom.

Map Decay → feedback (near unity = rings forever; low = unpitched thump) and Damping → loop low-pass (palm-mute-like). Optionally scale both by velocity (harder = longer ring/less damping); keep velocity amounts low—it is touchy.

Compensate register: at equal feedback low notes ring longer than high notes, so key-track feedback up for high notes and adjust damping in the opposite direction so decay and brightness feel even across the scale.
steps.expect: Similar ring time and damping low vs high

steps.action: Experiment: feed other sounds as the exciter into the tuned delay for pitched resonant textures.

verification: C3 sounds at ~7.64 ms delay; an octave up uses half the delay.
Lowering decay shortens notes until unpitched; damping darkens without shortening much.
With compensation, high notes ring comparably long to low notes.
